usage: Scientific (of liquids passing through membranes) and figurative-intellectual: an idea or a mood 'permea' a text, an epoch, a society ('una cultura permeata di scetticismo'). Often passive with 'di'. Regular -are verb: 'pèrmeo' (stress on the first e). 'Pervadere' is the close synonym; 'impregnare' more physical.

examples.it: Un senso di precarietà permea tutto il romanzo.
examples.en: A sense of precariousness permeates the whole novel.

examples.it: L'acqua permeò lentamente lo strato di argilla.
examples.en: The water slowly permeated the layer of clay.

examples.it: La sua opera è permeata di una religiosità inquieta.
examples.en: His work is imbued with a restless religiosity.

en: to procure, to obtain (with effort); (procacciarsi) to get oneself (a living, clients)
usage: Literary-commercial verb for obtaining something through activity and effort, often reflexive: 'procacciarsi il cibo', 'procacciarsi clienti'; the 'procacciatore d'affari' is a business intermediary. Regular -are verb (procaccio, procacci). 'Procurare' is the neutral synonym; 'procacciare' adds the idea of hunting.

examples.it: Si procacciava da vivere con piccoli lavori occasionali.
examples.en: He earned his living with small odd jobs.

examples.it: L'agente procacciò all'azienda contratti in tutta Europa.
examples.en: The agent procured contracts for the company all over Europe.

examples.it: Chi ha bisogno di procacciarsi il cibo ogni giorno non ha tempo per la filosofia.
examples.en: Those who must hunt for food every day have no time for philosophy.

en: to divulge, to spread (secrets, rumours)
usage: Learned, juridical-journalistic verb for spreading information that should have stayed confidential ('propalare segreti d'ufficio'), with a nuance of indiscretion or malice. 'Divulgare' is neutral, 'spifferare' colloquial, 'propalare' formal and disapproving. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Qualcuno ha propalato il contenuto degli interrogatori alla stampa.
examples.en: Somebody leaked the content of the interrogations to the press.

examples.it: Propalava voci infondate sui colleghi per screditarli.
examples.en: He spread groundless rumours about his colleagues to discredit them.

examples.it: Il funzionario fu sospeso per aver propalato informazioni riservate.
examples.en: The official was suspended for having divulged confidential information.

en: to burst out; to break into (tears, laughter, applause)
usage: Literary-journalistic verb for a sudden, irrepressible outburst ('il pubblico proruppe in un applauso'); a close synonym of 'erompere', and the standard formal alternative to 'scoppiare a piangere/ridere'. Irregular like 'rompere': proruppi, prorotto (participle rare); auxiliary essere. The adjective 'prorompente' (exuberant) is common.

examples.it: Alla notizia la madre proruppe in singhiozzi.
examples.en: At the news the mother burst into sobs.

examples.it: Il pubblico è prorotto in una risata liberatoria.
examples.en: The audience burst into liberating laughter.

examples.it: Temo che, se glielo dici, prorompa in una delle sue sfuriate.
examples.en: I fear that if you tell him, he will burst into one of his rages.

en: to swarm, to teem; to spring up everywhere, to proliferate
usage: From the Latin 'pullulare' (to sprout): of living things multiplying and of places teeming with them ('la città pullula di turisti'); also of things springing up everywhere ('pullulano i negozi di telefonia'). Journalistic and literary; 'brulicare' stresses movement, 'pullulare' abundance and proliferation. Regular -are verb (pùllulo).

examples.it: Il quartiere pullula di locali alla moda.
examples.en: The neighbourhood is teeming with trendy bars.

examples.it: Nel dopoguerra pullularono i piccoli partiti.
examples.en: In the post-war period small parties sprang up everywhere.

examples.it: Temo che la rete pullulerà sempre di notizie false.
examples.en: I fear the internet will always be swarming with fake news.

en: to inform in detail, to brief; to compare, to equate
usage: Formal-administrative verb for giving a full account ('la ragguaglierò sugli sviluppi'), the noun being 'ragguaglio' (detailed report); the older sense of making equal or comparing survives in accounting ('interesse ragguagliato ad anno'). Regular -are verb. 'Informare' and 'aggiornare' are the everyday alternatives.

examples.it: Il ministro fu ragguagliato sulla situazione al confine.
examples.en: The minister was briefed on the situation at the border.

examples.it: Vi ragguaglierò non appena avrò notizie certe.
examples.en: I will bring you up to date as soon as I have reliable news.

examples.it: Il tasso è ragguagliato ad anno secondo la prassi bancaria.
examples.en: The rate is expressed on an annual basis according to banking practice.

en: to recognise, to identify; to see, to discern (in something)
patterns: ravvisare gli estremi di un reato
usage: Formal, juridical-journalistic verb: to identify a quality or a fact in something ('ravvisare gli estremi del reato', to find the elements of a crime; 'non ravviso alcun motivo per'). Also to recognise a person ('lo ravvisò dal passo'). Regular -are verb. 'Riconoscere' is neutral, 'scorgere' perceptual.

examples.it: Il pubblico ministero non ha ravvisato gli estremi del reato.
examples.en: The public prosecutor did not find the elements of a crime.

examples.it: In quella scelta molti ravvisarono un segnale di debolezza.
examples.en: Many saw in that choice a sign of weakness.

examples.it: Non ravviso alcuna contraddizione tra le due dichiarazioni.
examples.en: I see no contradiction between the two statements.

en: to balk, to resist stubbornly; (of animals) to kick back
usage: Literally of a mule or horse kicking against the spur; figuratively, and often with humour, of a person who resists every attempt to persuade them ('recalcitra all'idea di trasferirsi'). The adjective 'recalcitrante' is far more common than the verb. Regular -are verb (recàlcitro).

examples.it: Il mulo recalcitrava e non voleva attraversare il ponte.
examples.en: The mule was balking and refused to cross the bridge.

examples.it: Recalcitrò a lungo prima di accettare la nomina.
examples.en: He resisted for a long time before accepting the appointment.

examples.it: Per quanto recalcitri, dovrà firmare anche lui.
examples.en: However much he balks, he will have to sign too.

en: to cut off, to sever (cleanly); to break off (ties)
usage: Literary and technical verb for a clean cut with a blade: flowers, branches, a rope and, figuratively, ties and relationships ('recidere ogni legame con il passato'). 'Tagliare' is neutral, 'troncare' more abrupt, 'mozzare' for limbs. Irregular like 'decidere': recisi, reciso; the adjective 'reciso' also means curt, flat (un rifiuto reciso).

examples.it: Il giardiniere recise le rose appassite con un colpo secco.
examples.en: The gardener cut off the withered roses with a sharp snip.

examples.it: Con quella lettera recise ogni rapporto con la famiglia.
examples.en: With that letter he severed all ties with his family.

examples.it: Bisogna che il chirurgo recida il tendine danneggiato.
examples.en: The surgeon needs to sever the damaged tendon.

en: to rebuke, to reprimand sharply
usage: Formal verb for a stern reproof from a superior ('il giudice redarguì l'avvocato'). Conjugated with -isc- (redarguisco). 'Rimproverare' is the everyday term, 'ammonire' a warning, 'rimbrottare' a grumbling scolding; 'redarguire' is the sharpest and most official.

examples.it: Il presidente redarguì aspramente il deputato per le sue parole.
examples.en: The speaker sharply rebuked the deputy for his words.

examples.it: Fu redarguito davanti a tutti i colleghi.
examples.en: He was reprimanded in front of all his colleagues.

examples.it: Non voglio che tu lo redarguisca in pubblico: parlagli in privato.
examples.en: I don't want you to reprimand him in public: talk to him privately.

en: to redeem; to deliver (from sin, slavery, debt)
usage: Religious, moral and historical verb: Christ 'redime' humanity, a hero 'redime' the oppressed, a sinner 'si redime' (auxiliary essere); in old legal usage also to buy back a mortgaged property. Irregular: redensi, redento. 'Riscattare' is the secular synonym.

examples.it: Sperava di redimersi dagli errori del passato.
examples.en: He hoped to redeem himself from the mistakes of the past.

examples.it: Secondo la dottrina, Cristo redense l'umanità con il suo sacrificio.
examples.en: According to doctrine, Christ redeemed humanity with his sacrifice.

examples.it: Nessuna donazione potrà redimere un'intera vita di soprusi.
examples.en: No donation will be able to redeem an entire life of abuses.

en: to shine brightly, to glow; to stand out (of virtues)
usage: Aulic verb (Dante, Petrarch) for a brilliant light, extended to glory and virtue ('rifulse per il suo coraggio'), sometimes ironic today ('non ha certo rifulso per originalità'). Irregular and defective: passato remoto 'rifulsi', participle 'rifulso' rare; auxiliary essere or avere. 'Risplendere' is the neutral synonym.

examples.it: La luna rifulgeva sul mare calmo.
examples.en: The moon shone brightly on the calm sea.

examples.it: In quella battaglia rifulse il valore dei difensori.
examples.en: In that battle the valour of the defenders shone forth.

examples.it: Il suo discorso non ha certo rifulso per chiarezza.
examples.en: His speech certainly did not stand out for clarity.

en: to scold, to grumble at; to reproach
usage: Familiar and picturesque verb for a grumbling, ill-tempered scolding, typical of parents and grandparents ('la nonna lo rimbrottava per il disordine'); the noun is 'rimbrotto'. Milder and more domestic than 'redarguire' or 'rampognare'. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Lo rimbrottò per essere tornato tardi senza avvisare.
examples.en: She scolded him for coming home late without letting her know.

examples.it: Mi rimbrottava continuamente, ma con affetto.
examples.en: He was forever grumbling at me, but affectionately.

examples.it: Se lo rimbrotti ancora, finirà per non ascoltarti più.
examples.en: If you keep scolding him, he'll end up not listening to you any more.

en: to jeer at, to ridicule; to make fun of openly
usage: Intensive of 'beffare': to mock someone loudly and publicly, with a hint of cruelty ('sbeffeggiato dai compagni'); frequent in sports and political journalism. 'Deridere' is more neutral, 'schernire' more contemptuous, 'sfottere' colloquial. Regular -are verb (sbeffeggio, sbeffeggi).

examples.it: I tifosi avversari sbeffeggiarono il portiere per tutta la partita.
examples.en: The opposing fans jeered at the goalkeeper for the whole match.

examples.it: Il comico ha sbeffeggiato i politici di ogni schieramento.
examples.en: The comedian ridiculed politicians of every stripe.

examples.it: Non sopporto che si sbeffeggi chi ha il coraggio di tentare.
examples.en: I can't stand people jeering at those who have the courage to try.

en: to dismay, to stun; (sbigottirsi) to be dumbfounded
usage: To leave someone speechless with shock or dismay; the participle 'sbigottito' ('rimase sbigottito') is the most used form. Conjugated with -isc- (sbigottisco); transitive with avere, intransitive and pronominal with essere. 'Sconvolgere' is stronger, 'stupire' weaker, 'sbigottire' adds bewilderment and fear.

examples.it: La notizia sbigottì l'intero paese.
examples.en: The news stunned the whole village.

examples.it: Restammo sbigottiti davanti a tanta crudeltà.
examples.en: We were dumbfounded by such cruelty.

examples.it: È sbigottita nel vedere quanto era cambiato.
examples.en: She was stunned to see how much he had changed.

en: to sound (the depths); to probe, to explore thoroughly
usage: Nautical term (to measure depth with a 'scandaglio', sounding line) used figuratively for probing minds, texts or situations in depth ('scandagliare le intenzioni dell'avversario'). Journalistic and literary; 'sondare' is the near synonym, 'esplorare' more general. Regular -are verb (scandaglio, scandagli).

examples.it: I sommozzatori scandagliarono il fondale per ore.
examples.en: The divers sounded the seabed for hours.

examples.it: Il romanzo scandaglia con lucidità le contraddizioni della borghesia.
examples.en: The novel probes the contradictions of the bourgeoisie with lucidity.

examples.it: Prima di decidere, vorrei che scandagliassimo ogni alternativa.
examples.en: Before deciding, I would like us to explore every alternative thoroughly.

en: to mock, to scorn; to deride contemptuously
usage: Literary verb for contemptuous mockery ('scherniva la sua fede'); the noun 'scherno' ('fatto oggetto di scherno') is common in formal prose. Conjugated with -isc- (schernisco). 'Deridere' is neutral, 'sbeffeggiare' loud and public, 'schernire' cold and disdainful.

examples.it: I soldati schernivano il prigioniero.
examples.en: The soldiers were mocking the prisoner.

examples.it: Fu schernito dai colleghi per le sue idee.
examples.en: He was scorned by his colleagues for his ideas.

examples.it: Chi schernisce i deboli rivela solo la propria miseria.
examples.en: Whoever mocks the weak reveals only his own wretchedness.

en: to hang out (washing); to reel off, to parade (knowledge, figures)
usage: Literally to hang out laundry to dry in the sun (Tuscan); figuratively and ironically, to display a long series of names, figures or citations to impress ('sciorinare statistiche'). Regular -are verb. 'Snocciolare' is the close colloquial synonym; 'ostentare' more general.

examples.it: Il ministro sciorinò una serie di cifre a memoria.
examples.en: The minister reeled off a series of figures from memory.

examples.it: La nonna sciorinava le lenzuola sul terrazzo.
examples.en: Grandmother would hang the sheets out on the terrace.

examples.it: Ha sciorinato citazioni in latino per mezz'ora.
examples.en: He paraded Latin quotations for half an hour.

en: to whip, to lash; to lash out at (with words); (of wind) to buffet
usage: From 'sferza' (whip): literally to lash, figuratively of biting satire or reproach ('sferzare i costumi del tempo') and of wind, rain or hail beating on something. Journalistic-literary; 'frustare' is the physical verb, 'fustigare' the moral one, 'sferzare' both. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Un vento gelido sferzava le facce dei pescatori.
examples.en: An icy wind lashed the fishermen's faces.

examples.it: Il commediografo sferzò i vizi della nobiltà con feroce ironia.
examples.en: The playwright lashed the vices of the nobility with ferocious irony.

examples.it: Temo che la stampa lo sferzi ancora più duramente dopo questa gaffe.
examples.en: I fear the press will lash him even harder after this blunder.

en: to incite secretly, to stir up; to instigate (to revolt)
usage: Spregiativo verb for whipping people up to disorder by underhand means; a 'sobillatore' is an agitator. Compared with 'istigare' (neutral-juridical) and 'aizzare' (open, violent), 'sobillare' implies secret and persistent manoeuvring behind the scenes. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Furono accusati di aver sobillato la folla contro il governatore.
examples.en: They were accused of having stirred up the crowd against the governor.

examples.it: Qualcuno sobilla gli operai per far saltare la trattativa.
examples.en: Somebody is stirring up the workers to wreck the negotiation.

examples.it: Non credo che li abbia sobillati lui: la rabbia era già diffusa.
examples.en: I don't think he incited them: the anger was already widespread.

en: to subjugate, to subdue; to dominate (a person, an audience)
usage: From 'giogo' (yoke): historical-political for conquering and subjecting peoples, and psychological for the dominating power of a personality or a gaze ('soggiogato dal suo fascino'). 'Sottomettere' is neutral, 'assoggettare' formal, 'soggiogare' the most vivid. Regular -are verb with -ghi/-ghe spelling.

examples.it: Roma soggiogò le tribù galliche in meno di dieci anni.
examples.en: Rome subjugated the Gallic tribes in less than ten years.

examples.it: Era soggiogato dalla personalità del maestro.
examples.en: He was under the spell of the master's personality.

examples.it: Nessun oratore soggiogherà mai una platea così scettica.
examples.en: No orator will ever dominate such a sceptical audience.

en: to overwhelm, to overpower; to exceed; to oppress
usage: Literary verb for a force that exceeds and crushes another: an army, a wave, a feeling ('soverchiato dal dolore'), or an overbearing person who bullies ('soverchieria' is bullying). 'Sopraffare' is the neutral synonym, 'sovrastare' just to tower over. Regular -are verb (soverchio, soverchi).

examples.it: Le forze nemiche soverchiavano di gran lunga le nostre.
examples.en: The enemy forces far outnumbered ours.

examples.it: Fu soverchiato da un'emozione che non riuscì a controllare.
examples.en: He was overwhelmed by an emotion he could not control.

examples.it: Non permettere che i più forti soverchino i più deboli.
examples.en: Don't allow the stronger to bully the weaker.

en: to compromise, to come to terms; to make concessions
usage: Juridical verb (to settle a dispute by mutual concession, 'transazione') that in ordinary formal usage appears mostly in the negative: 'su questo non transigo' (I won't compromise on this). Irregular: passato remoto 'transigei' or 'transigetti', participle 'transatto', practically used only in legal texts.

examples.it: Sulla sicurezza dei lavoratori non transigo.
examples.en: On workers' safety I make no compromises.

examples.it: Le parti transigettero la lite prima dell'udienza.
examples.en: The parties settled the dispute before the hearing.

examples.it: È un uomo che non transigerebbe mai sui principi.
examples.en: He is a man who would never compromise on principles.

en: to be astounded, to be amazed beyond words
usage: Expressive verb (literally 'to go out of the century', out of the world) for total astonishment, often with a comic tone ('trasecolò nel vedere il conto'). Regular -are verb; auxiliary essere or avere. Stronger than 'stupirsi'; 'strabiliare' and 'sbalordire' are the near synonyms, 'trasecolare' the most bookish.

examples.it: Trasecolai quando seppi che aveva lasciato tutto per fare il pescatore.
examples.en: I was astounded when I learned he had left everything to become a fisherman.

examples.it: I genitori sono trasecolati davanti alla pagella.
examples.en: The parents were dumbfounded at the report card.

examples.it: C'è da trasecolare a sentire certe dichiarazioni.
examples.en: It's enough to make you gasp, hearing certain statements.

en: to cherish (a dream, an idea); to long for, to contemplate fondly
usage: Literary verb (from 'vago' in the old sense of lovely) for dwelling lovingly on a desired image or plan, often unrealistic ('vagheggiava un ritorno alla terra'). More dreamy than 'desiderare', more nostalgic than 'sognare'; frequently ironic in journalism. Regular -are verb (vagheggio, vagheggi).

examples.it: Da giovane vagheggiava una carriera da esploratore.
examples.en: As a young man he cherished dreams of a career as an explorer.

examples.it: Alcuni vagheggiano ancora un impossibile ritorno alla lira.
examples.en: Some still fondly contemplate an impossible return to the lira.

examples.it: Vagheggiando un futuro che non sarebbe mai arrivato, lasciò passare il presente.
examples.en: Dreaming of a future that would never come, he let the present slip by.

en: to prophesy, to foretell (often ironically)
usage: Learned verb (from 'vate', the inspired poet-seer) for solemn prophecy, nearly always ironic in modern usage about pundits and economists who 'vaticinano' catastrophes. 'Predire' and 'prevedere' are neutral, 'profetizzare' religious, 'vaticinare' pompous. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Gli analisti vaticinavano il crollo della moneta unica.
examples.en: Analysts were prophesying the collapse of the single currency.

examples.it: Chi aveva vaticinato la fine del libro di carta si è dovuto ricredere.
examples.en: Those who had foretold the end of the paper book have had to think again.

examples.it: Non vaticinerei sventure prima di vedere i dati.
examples.en: I wouldn't prophesy disaster before seeing the data.

en: to harass, to oppress; to bully (with abuse of power)
usage: Formal-juridical verb for persistent ill-treatment by someone in a position of power (a tax authority, a landlord, an employer); the noun 'vessazione' and the adjective 'vessatorio' ('clausole vessatorie', unfair contract terms) are standard legal vocabulary. 'Angariare' is its more literary twin, 'tormentare' the everyday word. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: I contribuenti si sentono vessati da una burocrazia opprimente.
examples.en: Taxpayers feel harassed by an oppressive bureaucracy.

examples.it: Il caporale vessava le reclute con punizioni assurde.
examples.en: The corporal bullied the recruits with absurd punishments.

examples.it: Se continueranno a vessarci con controlli pretestuosi, ci rivolgeremo al giudice.
examples.en: If they keep harassing us with spurious inspections, we will go to court.
